request.spec:
An OPEN claim can no longer be edited; only a DRAFT can, and the edit of an open claim is refused
with an error on the claim. To change an open claim, void it and add a new one. A voided claim now
keeps its number (it is still never reused), and CLAIM_VOIDED carries it.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
An OPEN claim can no longer be edited; only a DRAFT can, and the edit of an open claim is refused
with an error on the claim. To change an open claim, void it and add a new one. A voided claim now
keeps its number (it is still never reused), and CLAIM_VOIDED carries it.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The change is in, and all 4 acceptance tests pass under `bin/e2e`.

**Server** (`claim/ClaimService.java`)
- Only a DRAFT claim can now be edited. Editing a claim in any other status (OPEN, SETTLED or VOID) is refused with a 409 conflict. Nothing is written to the store or the audit file.
- A voided claim now keeps its number. Numbers come from the sheet's running counter, so they are still never reused. The `CLAIM_VOIDED` record carries `number=N` because the claim still has one. A draft that was never opened has no number, so voiding it writes no number field.
- I merged the two audit-record helpers into one, since nothing needs to pass a different number any more. I also updated the comment on `Claim.number` to say the number is kept on void.

**Front end** (`features/claims/person-claims.ts`)
- Pressing Edit on a claim that isn't a draft opens no editor. Instead the claim's row shows an error (`claim-error`): "Only a draft claim can be edited; void an open claim and add a new one."
- If the server still refuses a save with a 409 (for example, another user opened the claim in the meantime), the same error appears on that claim's row and the editor stays open.
- Submitting the form again now clears that error.

The database schema didn't need to change. One thing to know: claims voided before this change already had their numbers cleared, so they will still show no number.
